acceptance_evidence: Resolved in cef7f032a (pre-existing on this branch) — getEmailAssetsBucket() restored to read process.env.PUBLIC_ASSETS_BUCKET_NAME with a prod fallback. Note: this fix commit landed at 21:18:38Z, before RazumRu's review was submitted at 21:40:34Z — the review's diff view was anchored to the stale commit 8ac7ee0a (19:57:40Z) and still showed the broken code.
description: getEmailAssetsBucket() hardcoded the prod GCS bucket name and dropped the previous process.env.PUBLIC_ASSETS_BUCKET_NAME override, while its JSDoc still claimed to read from the env var. This meant dev/UAT digest drafts would embed image URLs pointing at the prod bucket.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 29ee0c628 — the entire AI-generated-footer disclaimer block (and its generatedAt/timeZone/footerNoteStyle plumbing) was removed rather than recolored, so the contrast issue became moot.
description: The footer disclaimer rendered at a 2.52:1 contrast ratio (T.textVeryFaint on white), well under the WCAG AA 4.5:1 threshold for normal text. Product-decision styling/accessibility finding, marked Decided in the comment body.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — weekStart is now pinned once at dispatch time and threaded through ClientDigestJobData as weekStartIso; the processor derives weekStart from job.data.weekStartIso instead of recomputing Date.now()-7d. Verified present in the final merged code.
description: weekStart was computed as new Date(Date.now() - 7d) at job-execution time rather than at dispatch/enqueue time. Because the processor runs with concurrency: 5, early- and late-executing jobs from the same fan-out could compute different week windows, causing the digest content window to drift by hours relative to the dispatch-time filter.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 63a3eae4a — added limit: MAX_DISPATCH_PAIRS (10k) with orderBy lastMessageAt DESC (most-recently-active pairs kept first) plus a logger.warn when the cap is hit.
description: em.find(CrUserView, ...) in the dispatch processor had no limit on an unbounded, growing result set (all attorney/client pairs with recent messages), risking an OOM on the Cloud Run worker as Case Radar usage grows.

acceptance_evidence: Explicitly deferred — reply: 'Deferring to a follow-up — won't fix in this PR,' reasoning that React Email's JSX auto-escaping, encodeMimeHeader's base64 encoding, and the Zod .max() bounds already narrow the realistic injection surface. No code change made.
description: LLM-generated subject/body text flows into an attorney's Gmail draft without post-LLM validation, so a crafted client email in the COMMUNICATIONS context could attempt to steer the generated draft content (prompt injection), even though HTML/MIME-header injection itself is blocked by existing escaping.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — MIME helpers extracted to gmail-mime.util.ts; gmail-draft.service.spec.ts rewritten with vi.mock('googleapis') to exercise createDraft's real public behavior plus all 3 SA-JSON constructor failure modes (9 service tests + 11 helper tests).
description: createDraft() is the sole write surface of the whole client-digest feature (the call that actually creates the Gmail draft) yet had zero direct test coverage; the existing spec only exercised private __testing-exported helpers, not the public method.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — the __testing export was removed from gmail-draft.service.ts; the old protocol-level assertions moved to gmail-mime.util.spec.ts (testing the now-public util) and the service spec was rewritten to mock googleapis and assert on createDraft directly.
description: The gmail-draft service spec tested through a private __testing export rather than the public createDraft surface, so createDraft could be deleted entirely and all four tests would still pass — a test backdoor that doesn't actually guard the shipped behavior.

acceptance_evidence: Explicitly deferred — reply: 'Deferring — won't fix in this PR,' citing the dispatcher's small size, attempts: 1, and a recoverable same-week-miss failure mode as not yet worth mock-heavy coverage; thread marked resolved without a code change.
description: The dispatch processor's fan-out logic (flagByAttorney cache, null-attorney skip, per-pair feature-flag gating) had zero test coverage, so a bug that silently drops or duplicates an attorney/client pair would only surface in production on a Monday morning.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 63a3eae4a — both InternalServerErrorException throws in gmail-draft.service.ts (constructor SA-JSON failure and the drafts.create no-id case) now pass structured { message, ...context } objects per the api.mdc convention.
description: gmail-draft.service.ts threw InternalServerErrorException with a bare string message in two places, violating the project convention of always passing a structured object with message plus contextual identifiers, which hampers production debugging.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 63a3eae4a — added CLIENT_DIGEST_DISPATCH_CRON (default '0 16 * * 5') and CLIENT_DIGEST_DISPATCH_TZ (default America/New_York) to api.schema.ts, all three tfvars, and .env.example; the producer now reads them via env.getOrThrow(...).
description: The weekly dispatch cron pattern ('0 14 * * 1') was hardcoded as a constant instead of read from env, unlike the rest of Case Radar's cron config — meaning any schedule change would require a code commit and redeploy.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — all three local formatFullName helpers (template, LLM service, processor) replaced with the existing getFullName from @/shared/utils/format.
description: formatFullName was independently duplicated in three files (plus similar clientHandle/toCommunications/toParticipant helpers) despite an existing shared getFullName utility with 11 other callers, violating the project's 'shared utils over privates' convention.

acceptance_evidence: No reply thread found, and no fix present in the final merged code (997c86fbda9): digest-queue.processor.ts still calls timelineService.findByUser with perPage: 1000 and never checks timeline.meta.total/totalCount for truncation; the suggested TimelineService.findForDigest was never added.
description: findByUser is called with perPage: 1000 and orders messageAt DESC, so a high-volume client's older messages within the 7-day digest window are silently dropped from the LLM context with no detection or logging of the truncation.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — the new gmail-mime.util rejects CR/LF in raw-inserted addresses via a guardAddress helper, and encodeMimeHeader now also encoded-words ASCII display names containing RFC 5322 atom-specials (e.g. 'Smith, John <addr>' round-trips as one mailbox).
description: MIME header construction inserted To:/From: addresses raw with no CRLF/control-char guard, and encodeMimeHeader only base64-encoded non-ASCII text, so an ASCII display name containing RFC 5322 special characters (e.g. a comma) would produce a malformed From: header.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — added 3 indirect tests in digest-queue.processor.spec.ts covering the null-senderEmail/senderPartyType drop, the STAFF-based isFromAttorney derivation, and the zero-communications early-exit.
description: The toCommunications filter (which drops entries with null senderEmail/senderPartyType and derives isFromAttorney from the STAFF enum) and the communications.length === 0 early-exit in processJob both had no test coverage.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — added a round-trip equality assertion on the happy path, nextWeekItems.max(6) and needsFromClient.max(6) upper-bound tests, and extra-property rejection tests for the nested .strict() schemas.
description: The digest-content DTO spec had three gaps: no transformation guard on the happy path, an untested nextWeekItems.max(6) upper bound (asymmetric with the tested progressItems bound), and no extra-property rejection test for the nested .strict() ProgressItem/NeedsItem schemas.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — added two render-path tests: an empty needsFromClient renders the 'Nothing outstanding' copy instead of the section heading, and an all-unflagged digest renders no flag indicator.
description: The digest-template renderer spec never exercised the empty needsFromClient: [] state or an all-flagged:false digest — its fixture always included one flagged item and one needs item, leaving two render branches unverified.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 63a3eae4a — llm-processing.service.test.ts and digest-template.renderer.test.ts renamed to .spec.ts via a git mv-tracked rename.
description: Two new unit-test files used the .test.ts extension instead of the project's .spec.ts convention for unit tests (per .claude/rules/vitest.md and every sibling case-radar file).

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — dispatch-queue.types.ts and digest-queue.types.ts now hold types only; the runtime @Injectable() DI-token abstract classes and queue-name constants moved to new digest-queue.ts / dispatch-queue.ts files.

acceptance_evidence: Resolved in 04dfdfab7 — T.pageBg changed from #e8e6e2 to #edebe7 to match the --color-brown-50 oklch source value; the comment was updated to reference it.
description: T.pageBg ('#e8e6e2') was documented as mirroring the --color-brown-50 design token, but the actual oklch value resolves to approximately #edebe7 — a visible ~2% darker drift, with an incorrect comment.

acceptance_evidence: No reply thread found, and no fix present in the final merged code: llm-processing.service.ts still builds the exception message as `OpenAI refused to generate digest: ${message.refusal}`, so the raw refusal text is still concatenated into the surfaced error.
description: OpenAI's free-text refusal explanation (message.refusal) is concatenated directly into the thrown exception's message field; if error reporting or Bull Board surfaces 500-error bodies, this could leak paraphrased prompt fragments — a PII-adjacent exposure.

acceptance_evidence: No fix expected — the finding itself states it is 'flagged for visibility, not correction.'

acceptance_evidence: No reply thread found, and no fix present in the final merged code: the hero still has width="600" height="400" HTML attrs alongside the CSS style override, unchanged from review time.
description: The hero combines width="600"/height="400" HTML attributes with a style={{ width: '100%', height: 'auto' }} CSS override; old Outlook's Word-based renderer ignores inline CSS on and uses the HTML attrs verbatim, so the image would overflow once the card narrows below 600px.

acceptance_evidence: No reply thread found, and no fix present in the final merged code: FONT_STACK is still "'Hanken Grotesk', sans-serif", not aligned with the auth-template's richer fallback stack.
description: The digest template's font fallback is just 'Hanken Grotesk', sans-serif; most desktop email clients can't resolve the @import'd webfont, and the fallback is thinner than the richer system-font stack already used by the auth email template.
